inconsistencies: #36114 and #35358 solve the same problem (verifying/hardening PSBTs returned by external signers). Review #36114 first: it is the broader change (merge instead of replace, sighash rejection, revamped mock); #35358's output-count/amount/scriptPubKey equality checks should then be folded in or rebased on it.

#34457 and #34533 both route wallet rebroadcasts through private broadcast when -privatebroadcast is set. #34457 is a superset (initial sends plus rebroadcasts plus Qt exception handling); scope should be decided once and #34457 reviewed first, with #34533 reduced or closed.

Database chain, order matters: #33033 (SQLite statement RAII) and #32895 (client-version/feature recording) are prerequisites of #33034 (transactions table), which #27865 (no-longer-spendable TXO tracking) builds on. Reviewing #27865 or #33034 before the two bases is wasted effort.
Chain: #35998 (nodiscard WalletBatch write handling) is stated to depend on #35752 (atomic encryption state). #35752 must land first; both are P1.
#36300 backports #36230 to 32.x, and #36133 is based on #36230 — review #36230 once and let the backport follow; do not re-litigate the approach in #36300.
#35918, #36070 and #36143 are three separate prerequisites for the GUI multisig wizard (#35645). They should be sequenced together so the wizard is not blocked on the slowest one.
#35317 adds a one-off snake_case alias while reviewers want a project-wide RPC naming transition; the naming policy decision should be made before this PR or its replacement issue is acted on.
#31668, #36236 and #35224 all change importdescriptors semantics (skip rescan, verify balance, error payload); conflicts and overlapping help text are likely if they are reviewed in isolation.
#34698 converts AvailableCoins to util::Result, which overlaps the broader util::Result conversion in draft #25722 — the draft should rebase on whichever lands first.
result.notes: Wallet has an unusually large correctness tail: the P1/upper-P2 block is dominated by fund-safety, database-corruption and rescan-correctness fixes, and these are ordered ahead of the two large feature programmes (silent payments, private broadcast) deliberately, following the category's 'fund safety, then backup/recovery/migration, then privacy, then features' ordering rather than by feature size. The P3 band is large; within it, user-visible bugs are placed first, then privacy/UX features, then prerequisites for the multisig wizard, then tests and internal refactors.
